raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

#43584 moved the 2-rank IPC all-to-all's exported buffers and the N-rank `_PipelinePool` onto `ipc_shareable_zeros`, but the N-rank transport's signal flags, timeout flag and exchange staging (from #43164) stayed plain `torch.zeros`. Under `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` those can land in expandable segments, whose IPC import calls `pidfd_getfd`. Containers without ptrace rights deny that syscall with EPERM.

Seen on a RunPod 4xB300 container (2026-10-22): every sequence-parallel server with more than two ranks logged `IPC all-to-all (multi-rank) unavailable (pidfd_getfd: Operation not permitted); using NCCL` (24 warnings across 6 runs: Wan2.2-A14B, Cosmos3, MiniMax-H3 4-GPU), so the copy-engine all-to-all and the head-grouped pipelined attention never ran.

It can also hang. Whether a plain `torch.zeros` buffer lands in an expandable block depends on each rank's allocator history, so one rank can import its peer's flags while the other fails. Init then deadlocks: one rank waits in `_share(timed_out)`'s `all_gather_object`, the other in the all-reduce where ranks agree on the outcome, until the NCCL watchdog aborts both (~10 min). On RunPod all four ranks happened to fail alike, which is why only the fallback was visible.

## Modifications

- `ipc_a2a_multi.py`: the signal flags, timeout flag and staging buffers come from `ipc_shareable_zeros`, like every other exported buffer. If sharing the flags still fails, the init error now says so.
- `ipc_a2a.py`: one docstring line on why `ipc_shareable_zeros` matters (`pidfd_getfd`).
- The NCCL fallback for hosts that genuinely cannot do CUDA IPC is unchanged.

Tests:
- `test/unit/test_ipc_a2a_lifecycle.py` (CPU, mocked): every buffer the N-rank path exports must come from `ipc_shareable_zeros`. On main the flags, timeout flag and staging fail it.
- `single_test_file/test_ipc_a2a_multi_gpu.py`: reruns the 2-rank multi-rank worker with `expandable_segments:True` under a seccomp filter that makes `pidfd_getfd` fail with EPERM.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerical change: the same buffers, allocated outside expandable segments.

On 2xH200 with `pidfd_getfd` blocked by seccomp (reproduces the RunPod warning exactly):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| multi-rank worker, expandable segments on, syscall allowed | passes, 3 `pidfd_getfd` calls | passes, 0 calls |
| pipelined-attention test, syscall blocked | RunPod warning on both ranks, FAIL | PASS, 0 calls |
| new 2-GPU test, syscall blocked | deadlock (713 s, watchdog) | PASS (~36 s) |
| 2-rank IPC test, syscall blocked | PASS, 0 calls | PASS, 0 calls |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Restores the IPC all-to-all on such hosts; the multi-rank GPU test file runs in ~48 s on H200, unchanged. Follow-up (not in this PR): `runtime/distributed/ipc_cuda.py` (scheduler↔client CUDA IPC) has the same exposure on the import side.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

 from __future__ import annotations
 
+import ctypes
+import errno
 import os
 import subprocess
 import sys
@@ -45,6 +47,35 @@ def _attend_rows(q, k, v):
     ).to(q.dtype)
 
 
+def _deny_pidfd_getfd() -> None:
+    """Fail pidfd_getfd with EPERM in this process, as containers without ptrace
+    rights do; importing an expandable-segment IPC handle needs it."""
+
+    class Insn(ctypes.Structure):  # struct sock_filter
+        _fields_ = [
+            ("code", ctypes.c_uint16),
+            ("jt", ctypes.c_uint8),
+            ("jf", ctypes.c_uint8),
+            ("k", ctypes.c_uint32),
+        ]
+
+    class Prog(ctypes.Structure):  # struct sock_fprog
+        _fields_ = [("len", ctypes.c_uint16), ("filter", ctypes.POINTER(Insn))]
+
+    insns = (Insn * 4)(
+        Insn(0x20, 0, 0, 0),  # load the syscall number
+        Insn(0x15, 0, 1, 438),  # pidfd_getfd, the same number on every arch
+        Insn(0x06, 0, 0, 0x00050000 | errno.EPERM),  # SECCOMP_RET_ERRNO
+        Insn(0x06, 0, 0, 0x7FFF0000),  # SECCOMP_RET_ALLOW
+    )
+    libc = ctypes.CDLL(None, use_errno=True)
+    # PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS, then PR_SET_SECCOMP with SECCOMP_MODE_FILTER
+    if libc.prctl(38, 1, 0, 0, 0) or libc.prctl(
+        22, 2, ctypes.byref(Prog(len(insns), insns)), 0, 0
+    ):
+        raise OSError(ctypes.get_errno(), "could not install the seccomp filter")
+
+
 def _worker() -> int:
     import torch.distributed as dist

+
+    agreed = MagicMock()

+    with (
+        patch(f"{_MULTI}.ipc_shareable_zeros", side_effect=shareable_zeros),
+        patch(f"{_MULTI}.torch.zeros"),
+        patch(f"{_MULTI}.torch.tensor", return_value=agreed),
+        patch(f"{_MULTI}.torch.cuda.current_device", return_value=0),
+        patch(f"{_MULTI}.torch.cuda.can_device_access_peer", return_value=True),
+        patch(f"{_MULTI}.torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing", return_value=False),
+        patch(f"{_MULTI}.dist.get_rank", return_value=0),
+        patch(f"{_MULTI}.dist.get_world_size", return_value=2),
+        patch(f"{_MULTI}.dist.all_reduce"),
+        patch(f"{_MULTI}._member_devices", return_value=[0, 1]),
+        patch(f"{_MULTI}._StreamMemOps"),
+        patch(f"{_MULTI}.load_ipc_a2a_sync"),
+        patch("ctypes.CDLL"),
+        patch.object(state, "_share", side_effect=share),
+    ):
+        state.init(object())
+        state.get_staging(8, torch.bfloat16)
+        _PipelinePool(state, torch.bfloat16, 8, 8, 2)
+    # flags, timeout flag, staging, pipeline receive/output boxes and counters
+    assert [any(t is s for s in shareable) for t in exported] == [True] * 7
